name: Bathroom Remodeling Timeline: From Demolition to Final Fixture Inspection

step.name: Step 1: Planning and Permitting
step.text: Before any physical work starts, your contractor verifies your proposed fixture layout against local building codes. Detailed plans for mechanical ventilation, electrical layout, and plumbing runs are drafted, and required building permits are formally submitted to your local building department. This phase typically takes one to three weeks depending on municipal review speeds.

step.name: Step 2: Safe Demolition and Framing Adjustments
step.text: Crews turn off water supplies and power before carefully removing old vanities, tubs, shower surrounds, and flooring down to the framing. The team inspects exposed wall studs and subflooring for hidden moisture or rot, completing needed structural repairs or framing adjustments for custom niches and curbless shower bases over several days.

step.name: Step 3: Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing Rough-Ins
step.text: Licensed trade professionals run new water supply lines, reposition drain stacks, install dedicated GFCI electrical circuits, and duct mechanical exhaust fans to the building exterior. Everything remains exposed in the wall cavities so local building inspectors can sign off on the rough mechanicals before any surfaces are enclosed.

step.name: Step 4: Shower Pan Testing and Waterproofing
step.text: The shower pan is installed and thoroughly leak-tested according to code standards to guarantee zero water penetration. Moisture-resistant backing boards and liquid or sheet waterproofing membranes are applied over shower enclosures and wet areas, ensuring complete protection behind all future tile surfaces.

step.name: Step 5: Tile Installation, Finish Carpentry, and Trim
step.text: Installers set wall and floor tile, marble details, grout, and sealants with careful precision. Once tile finishes cure, trim carpenters hang doors, casing, and molding, followed by high-moisture interior paint applied across ceilings and untiled wall spaces over the course of three to five days.

step.name: Step 6: Fixture Installation and Final Inspections
step.text: Plumbers install toilets, vanity sinks, and shower valves while electricians trim out light fixtures and exhaust fan switches. The project concludes with a final inspection from the local building authority and a thorough walkthrough with your contractor to address every detail. What to Expect During the Process: Having a single lead contractor on-site keeps each phase moving seamlessly from framing to final tile.
